title: racosperma leptospermoides subsp. psammophilum
intro: Racosperma leptospermoides subsp. psammophilum, commonly known as the Coastal Rose, is a plant species endemic to Australia. It belongs to the family Fabaceae and is a shrub-like plant that is rich in medicinal properties. The Coastal Rose has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, and is believed to help in wound healing and reducing fever. The bioactive constituents of Racosperma leptospermoides subsp. psammophilum include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its therapeutic actions such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antiseptic properties.
